Each is the arm's mean absolute error of the member average minus the reference arm's, in points of capacity, over all leads. The level is 99.5%.

Id Technology Arm Reference C1 solar cams w C2 solar cams_stage0 cams C3 solar csr w C4 wind base_margin w C5, C6 solar, wind start_2023 w C7, C8 solar, wind start_2024 w C9 solar small_block w C10 wind speed_block w

Every table also gives the scores per technology and per lead band (0 to 24 h, 1 to 2 days, 3 to 6 days, 7 to 10 days, 11 to 15 days), with a note that the claims rest on 6 solar and 3 wind farms.

docs.title: Checks before the contrasts are read
docs.text:
• Reproduction. Arm w must reproduce experiment 00001's s1_memberavg score to within 0.05 points per technology. If not, the pipeline has changed and the experiment stops.
  • Leakage review. A reviewer reads the code for leakage, for every fit and for stage 0 stopping before 2025-06-17, and for the clear-sky constant and power curve using training rows only.
  • Stage 0 sanity. A fit that stops before 2025-05-06 is scored on the next 6 weeks (a block of valid times, not a random split, because one valid time recurs across leads), and its error against CAMS is printed beside the raw ENS shortwave's error.

docs.title: Resolution limit
docs.text: Nine series in two weather regions cannot resolve gains under about 0.3 points of capacity. Intervals are wide, and an equivalence is reported only when the interval lies inside -0.3 to +0.3.

docs.title: Where does Primary substation demand stand against the stored baselines?
docs.text:
We asked how well our best demand model forecasts Primary substations (substations that step power down to the local distribution network) compared with a stored baseline that uses the power at the same time in earlier weeks, and why the model now in production loses to that baseline. We scored an upgraded model (N1, an XGBoost quantile model trained on ensemble weather forecasts, with recent power as inputs), the production recipe (the stored xgboost_baseline), and the baseline on 16 Primary substations. The upgraded model was level with the baseline, with an interval that includes zero, and the production recipe lost to the baseline by 1.69 points of capacity.

Verdict: inconclusive. The upgraded XGBoost quantile model N1 does not beat manual_heuristic with an interval that excludes zero. For the 16 Primary substations, N1's mean absolute error of the median is 8.45 points of capacity over all leads against 8.23 for manual_heuristic: C1 is +0.22 (99% interval -0.54 to +0.97). Up to 48 hours N1 scores 7.38 against 7.95, which meets the planned 0.5-point size (-0.57) but not the interval (-1.33 to +0.27), and beyond 3 days N1 is level or worse (+0.40, -0.39 to +1.19). The production recipe does lose to manual_heuristic, by +1.69 points (C3, +0.98 to +2.59), at every lead and in 12 of 16 series. The hypothesis named a mechanism for that loss, no usable power persistence at short leads, and the equal gap at every lead contradicts it. The decision rule has no branch for this outcome, so the verdict and the gate action below are the fall-through reading of the rule and were not pre-registered. The gate for P7 and P8 is not passed, so P7 compares the staged chain with manual_heuristic as well as with N1. A point is 1% of the series' effective capacity. The substations are not named. manual_heuristic is a stored baseline that forecasts from the power at the same time of day in earlier weeks and years. The mean absolute error of the median is the average gap between the median forecast and the measured power.

docs.title: What the arms score
docs.text:
Every arm is scored on the same 768,073 cases per seed (Primary substations; 965,723 cases for all 20 series), on the 73 runs of fold_a_every5d_v1. Intervals resample whole months and the three seeds; the stored baselines have no seed, so each is repeated three times.

Arm All leads Up to 48 h 3 days or more manual_heuristic 8.23 7.95 8.31 N1 8.45 7.38 8.71 N1 without lagged power 9.60 9.19 9.71 Stage 1 trained on ERA5 (S1) 9.48 9.07 9.59 Production recipe 9.92 9.65 10.02 climatology 10.33 10.19 10.36

N1 is no better than manual_heuristic on the quantile score. The quantile score (an estimate of the continuous ranked probability score) is 5.89 for manual_heuristic, 6.33 for N1 (C1 +0.44, -0.27 to +1.08), 9.52 for the production recipe, and 7.46 for climatology. For the two bulk supply points N1 scores 11.3 against 12.3 for manual_heuristic, and for the two grid supply points 27.4 against 29.8, on the error of the median; two series per type resolve no interval.

docs.title: Why the production recipe loses to manual_heuristic
docs.text:
The gap is the same size at every lead, so it does not come from missing persistence at short leads. C3 is between +1.60 and +1.79 in every lead band, and the production recipe is worse in all 12 months. Two hypotheses are consistent with the numbers; the experiment did not isolate either.

  • A level offset. Every arm forecasts the validation year too low (figure 3). The mean error of the median is -2.3 points for the production recipe and -1.3 for manual_heuristic. The N1 arms trained on April 2024 to June 2025, and manual_heuristic may track the drift because it copies the last weeks of observed power. Post hoc, subtracting each arm's own per-series mean error (an oracle, since it uses the validation year) lowers the production recipe's error to 8.95 and manual_heuristic's to 7.87, so the offset accounts for 0.6 of the 1.69 points. The offset is not specific to the production recipe: climatology (-2.9) and S1 (-3.1) are lower still.
  • No recent power. The remaining 1.1 points are of the size that lagged power recovers in N1 (C4, 1.15, -2.16 to -0.58), but C4 compares two N1 arms and not the production recipe. N1 without lagged power scores 9.60, 0.32 below the production recipe (E7, 95% interval -0.76 to +0.27), so the quantile loss, the 00006 columns, the recency weights, and training on ENS pooled over members lowered the error by an amount not distinguishable from zero.

docs.title: Other findings
docs.text:
• N1 without lagged power does no better than S1 on the error of the median (C5 +0.12, -0.41 to +0.61), so training on ENS instead of ERA5 changes that error by less than the interval can show. On the quantile score N1 without lagged power is better (C5 -0.73, -1.14 to -0.31, 11 of 12 months). The planned clause that N1 without lags recovers half the production gap beyond 3 days fails: C5 is +0.13 against C3's +1.71.
  • Pooling the 51 members helps slightly. N1 beats the control member alone by 0.05 points (E3, 95% interval -0.08 to -0.03).
  • The calendar columns matter little. Removing hour, weekday, and days to Christmas raises the error by 0.17 (E4, +0.09 to +0.25) and does not change the quantile score (+0.01).
  • N1 beats 00005's ENS-trained model with lags as inputs by 0.50 points (E5, -0.64 to -0.36), from lags measured at the origin instead of nullified at short leads.

docs.title: Post hoc
docs.text: The oracle level correction is post hoc. The plan pre-registered a decomposition of the production gap by bias; the oracle correction was added after the verdict, uses the validation year to estimate the offset, and changes no pre-registered contrast. A deployable version, a correction from the last 14 days of observed error, is a candidate for P8.

docs.title: Limits
docs.text:
• The telemetry delay is assumed. Every N1 result is conditional on the newest usable value being 3.5 hours before the origin.
  • N1 trained on 15 months, not from 2023-09, because the stored ENS archive starts on 2024-04-01. C5 mixes ENS against ERA5 training with the shorter window, and S1 trains on 2023-09 onward.
  • 16 series and 12 months leave 99% intervals of about plus or minus 0.8 points, wider than the planned 0.5-point effect.

docs.title: Plan, written before any code ran
Plan: sizing
docs.text:
• Stored data: prediction sets only, under data/ml-experiments/; no production table changes.
  • Production serving path: not touched.
  • Degradation rule: not touched.
  • Defensible designs: more than one. N1's weather pooling, the telemetry delay, and the lag definitions are choices; each is fixed below before a fit.
  • Callers: the scripts copy 00005's helpers and read its stored predictions, which the author of this plan could name without searching.

Size: complex. The plan gets two Sonnet reviews (Opus is kept for work that is truly vital), the code gets two Sonnet reviews (leakage and the fit stopping at train_end; then correctness), and the write-up gets one.

docs.title: Plan: arms
docs.text:
All arms are scored on the 73 runs of fold_a_every5d_v1, on the rows every arm holds and an observed power value, for valid times before 2026-07-01. Primary substations (16 series) are the headline; BSP and GSP (2 series each) are reported separately and never averaged in.

  • MH, CL, PROD (stored): manual_heuristic, climatology, and the production recipe (xgboost_baseline, fold mid_2025_to_mid_2026) read from the power_forecasts Delta table; the quantiles of each arm's members. They have no seed, so each is repeated once per seed.
  • S1 (00005's r0_from2023): stage 1, ERA5-trained from 2023-09, no lags, pooled over the 51 members. R1 (r1) and R2 (r2) are reported as references.
  • N1: one XGBoost model per series with the 9-level quantile loss, trained on the ENS control member of every daily run from 2024-04-01 (the start of the stored ENS archive, so 2023-09 is not available to ENS-trained arms), valid times up to 2025-06-30 23:30. Columns: the 00006 Primary set (weather block, solar position, hour, weekday, COVID indicator, windowed days to Christmas), the lead in hours, and three lags measured from the forecast origin. Recency weights use a half-life of 2 years, anchored at 2025-06-30 (the last training valid time), not at each row's own date. The fit runs a fixed 500 rounds with no early stopping and no validation split. A training row is kept only when its valid time is on or before 2025-06-30 23:30, and every lag of a training row lies before that row's origin.
  • Pooling. The 51 members' 9 quantiles each give 459 values with equal member weights and the 9-level atom masses; the forecast quantiles are the weighted quantiles of those values at the 9 levels, sorted so none cross. A model trained on the control member and applied to perturbed members adds its own spread to the ensemble's spread, so the bands may be too wide, which raises the quantile score. N1-control, N1 applied to the control member alone, checks this (exploratory).
  • N1-nolag: N1 without the lag columns (isolates the lags, and ENS-trained against ERA5-trained once compared with S1).
  • N1-nocal: N1 without hour, weekday, and days to Christmas (the no-calendar control).

The three lags. The origin T is the NWP run time plus 9 hours. The newest usable observation is the latest half-hour at or before T minus 3.5 hours. NGED's files cover 6-hour windows, and the live ingest downloads each window 3 hours after it ends, so at 09:00 UTC the 03:00 to 06:00 window has just arrived. The plan keeps one half-hour of margin, so the newest value is the one stamped 05:30. The lags are the power at that newest half-hour, the power at the latest earlier time with the same half-hour of day as the valid time, and the power at the latest earlier time with the same weekday and half-hour. All three are zero-lookahead by construction. The telemetry delay is an assumption, not a measurement of NGED's delay; the live ingest's download time is the only evidence in the repository. Every N1 result is conditional on the 3.5-hour figure, and no sensitivity run is planned.

Deviation from P6. P6 names a 2023-09 start for N1. The stored ENS archive starts on 2024-04-01, so N1 trains on 15 months where S1 trains on 22. C5 therefore mixes the effect of training on ENS with the effect of the shorter window. The stored arms have no seed, so each is repeated once per seed as the skill requires; the three copies are identical, and the intervals resample months.

Diagnosis of the production gap. The stored forecasts are split by lead band and series; the gap between production and manual_heuristic is decomposed into bias (mean error) and the rest; and the ladder PROD, S1, N1-nolag, N1 shows which step recovers the gap.

docs.title: Plan: planned contrasts (99%, Primary substations)
docs.text:
• C1: N1 minus manual_heuristic (primary).
  • C2: N1 minus PROD.
  • C3: PROD minus manual_heuristic (the gap to diagnose).
  • C4: N1 minus N1-nolag (what origin lags add).
  • C5: N1-nolag minus S1 (ENS-trained quantile against ERA5-trained, both lag-free).

The planned contrasts are read at 99% over all leads, over leads up to 48 hours, and over leads of 3 days or more. Every other contrast is exploratory and read at 95%, including each lead band.

docs.title: Plan: past weather
docs.text: N1 uses ENS weather in training and in scoring, so no past weather is used at lag times. The lags are of power, observed before the origin.

docs.title: Does a stage 0 that maps ENS irradiance onto CAMS help the CAMS-trained demand model?
docs.text:
We asked whether correcting forecast sunlight before a demand model reads it improves the forecast. The demand model was trained on a satellite estimate of sunlight, but the weather forecasts it receives when it is used give more daytime sunlight than that estimate (281 against 263 watts per square metre, averaged over daytime). We mapped the forecast sunlight onto the satellite estimate, separately for each of the 51 ensemble members, and measured the change in error. The error fell by 0.067 points of capacity (1% of a series' effective capacity), but mismatches remained in individual months.

This experiment is P20 of the research plan, the follow-up to experiment 00009. Experiment 00009 found that a stage 1a trained on CAMS irradiance lowered the Primary quantile score by only 0.035 points when fed ENS shortwave, and measured the ENS daylight shortwave at 281 W/m² against 263 for CAMS. This experiment tests that offset as a cause. Stage 1a is an XGBoost model per series that turns weather into power. The quantile score measures how well the forecast quantiles fit what happened, and smaller is better.

docs.title: Size
docs.text:
• What gets stored: prediction sets and tables under this experiment's private folder. Nothing enters a Delta table.
  • Production serving path: not touched.
  • Degradation rule: not touched.
  • Designs that would test the hypothesis defensibly: three. Empirical quantile mapping, planned here, keeps the spread of the 51 members. A regression of CAMS on ENS would pull every member towards the conditional mean and shrink the spread. A single multiplicative factor would fix only the mean offset.
  • Callers that need searching for: none. The scripts live in this experiment's folder, and they reuse the code and the fitted models of 00009.

The only trigger that fires is the second design: the experiment adds a method that more than one design could implement. It therefore gets one review of the plan, one of the code, and one of the write-up, all by Sonnet. The earlier advice lists were read. This plan follows "Keep the stage 1a training weather in ERA5 until a CAMS-trained arm has been tried with the ENS shortwave bias-corrected" and "Score any irradiance-input change by lead band as well as in total" (00009), and sets its threshold of -0.03 points near the 97.5% half-width of 00009's C1 (0.035 points). A gain of that size is at the edge of what the rows can resolve.

docs.title: Design
docs.text:
No stage 1a model is refitted. The ERA5-trained and CAMS-trained boosters of 00009 (20 series, three seeds) are loaded as they are. Only the input they read at validation changes, so C2 differs from 00009's CAMS-trained arm in one input: the ENS shortwave column.

Stage 0 is an empirical quantile mapping from ENS shortwave to CAMS irradiance. The mapping is fitted on the training times before 2025-06-17 (14 days before the first validation run), from the stage 1 pilot's ENS training table (one ensemble member per run, 456 runs from 2024-04-01; the script prints which member and reports it, since the control member is not exchangeable with the perturbed ones), filtered to valid_time before 2025-06-17 (not to init time, because the table runs to 2025-06-30), with an assertion on the maximum valid time. The table holds 22 series, and the mapping uses only the 20 modelled ones paired with CAMS held half-hourly at the series' own point. The pairs are pooled over the 20 series and binned by lead band (the five bands of 00009) and by solar zenith (6 bins of equal cosine width, daylight only, zenith below 80°). Within a bin, 99 quantiles of the ENS values are matched to the same quantiles of the CAMS values, and the mapping is piecewise linear between them and clamped to the end points outside the fitted range. A bin with fewer than 1,000 pairs borrows the mapping of its neighbouring zenith bin. At validation, each member's value is mapped on its own, so the 51 members keep their spread. Night rows pass through unchanged. CAMS is needed only at training times, never at forecast time.

The stage 0 output is checked before stage 1a reads it. The mismatch table lists the mean daylight shortwave of CAMS, raw ENS, and corrected ENS by month of the validation year, with the ratio to CAMS, plus the mean spread of the 51 members before and after.

Two planned contrasts, kept separate, both on Primary substations over all leads. C1 is the CAMS-trained arm on raw ENS minus the ERA5-trained arm, recomputed here from 00009's models on the same rows; a value differing from 00009's -0.035 by more than 0.005 is reported and read as the noise floor of GPU prediction. C2 is the stage 0 contrast. The threshold of -0.03 is a little under the half-width of 00009's interval, so a gain of that size is at the edge of what the rows resolve.

Exploratory contrasts are read at 95%. They are: C2 for the four bulk supply point and grid supply point series together (the CAMS values exist for all 20 series, which 00009 used); C2 by lead band and for daylight and night separately; X1, a quantile mapping of ENS onto ERA5 shortwave at the same cells, fed to the ERA5-trained arm, minus that arm on raw ENS (does a stage 0 help whichever product stage 1a trained on); and C2 for each Primary series.

One post hoc variant, labelled as such. After the planned run showed monthly mismatches, X3 and X4 add a stage 0 fitted separately for each calendar month (same bins, same cutoff, and the all-year mapping where a month and lead band has too few pairs), applied to the CAMS-trained arm. The planned contrasts and the verdict rule are unchanged.

Leakage and calendar checks. Stage 0 sees no valid time from 2025-06-17 on. Stage 1a models are 00009's, trained before the same date. No calendar column is added.

Known limits. CAMS is held hourly while the ENS shortwave is interpolated to half-hours, which the marginal mapping ignores. The mapping is fitted on 14 months, is unconditional on the day's weather, and corrects the offset in distribution, not the forecast error of an individual member. The training table holds one member per run, assumed exchangeable with the other 50.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
The verdict is inconclusive by the pre-registered rule, although C2 itself beats the planned size. Stage 0 lowers the Primary quantile score of the CAMS-trained arm by 0.067 points of capacity (C2, 97.5% interval -0.094 to -0.039, half-width 0.028), more than the -0.03 the plan required, and in 12 of 12 months and 14 of 16 series. The rule also required that the corrected ENS shortwave stay within 5% of CAMS in every month, and the bias check failed. C2 is not a small gain: its interval lies wholly beyond the planned threshold, and only the bias check prevents a verdict of supported. C1 reproduces experiment 00009's -0.035 (-0.070 to +0.001) exactly, and the repeated raw-input quantiles differ from 00009's by 0.000 in every level over 3,074,760 rows each.

Arm Primary quantile score BSP GSP Primary error of the median ERA5-trained, raw ENS 7.88 (6.92 to 8.75) 8.60 21.08 9.49 CAMS-trained, raw ENS 7.84 (6.89 to 8.73) 8.56 20.98 9.46 CAMS-trained, stage 0 7.78 (6.84 to 8.64) 8.51 20.94 9.44 ERA5-trained, stage 0 (X1) 7.85 (6.91 to 8.73) 8.60 21.07 9.47 CAMS-trained, monthly stage 0 (post hoc, X3) 7.80 (6.87 to 8.66) 8.56 20.96 9.45 Climatology (00005's r2) 8.21 (7.45 to 8.97) 9.43 24.41 11.30

All scores are in points of capacity, over all leads, with 95% month-and-seed intervals for the Primary quantile score. The CAMS-trained arm with stage 0 is 0.102 points better than the ERA5-trained arm (-0.143 to -0.059), three times 00009's gain.

Stage 0 fixes the year's mean mismatch but not each month's. Over the validation year, the mean daylight ENS shortwave is 6.2% above CAMS as published and 0.0% above after stage 0 (320.9 and 302.1 against 302.1 W/m²). By month, the published ratio runs from 0.92 to 1.26, and after stage 0 from 0.81 (December) to 1.13 (July), so the 5% monthly bound failed. The member spread of the shortwave after stage 0 is 1.27 times its published value (1.13 to 1.31 by month), outside the 10% the plan expected.

The prediction was right on the size of the gain and wrong on its lead times and on the member spread. C2 fell inside the predicted 0.03 to 0.10 band, and the year's mean daylight ratio to CAMS reached 1.000. The predicted concentration in the first 6 days did not appear: the first day has the smallest gain (-0.038), and 7 to 15 days gain as much as 3 to 6 days. The member spread changed by 27% against a predicted 10%. The offset before correction was 6.2%, a little under the 7% that experiment 00009 reported.

The gain is in daylight and at every lead from 1 day on. In daylight the contrast is -0.168 (95% interval -0.229 to -0.114) and at night it is 0.000. By lead band it is -0.038 up to 1 day (-0.085 to +0.002), -0.084 for 1 to 2 days, -0.061 for 3 to 6 days, -0.068 for 7 to 10 days, and -0.075 for 11 to 15 days, so the gain does not fade at long leads as 00009's did. The interval for the first day reaches +0.002, so a gain there is probable and not resolved. Over the 4 bulk and grid supply point series together it is -0.042 (-0.086 to -0.001), too few series to say more. Stage 0 also helps the ERA5-trained arm (X1, -0.025, -0.038 to -0.012), so part of the gain is a general correction of the ENS shortwave, and the CAMS-trained arm gains 0.077 more than the ERA5-trained arm after both have stage 0 (X2, -0.111 to -0.040).

Post hoc, a monthly mapping did no better. Fitting one mapping per calendar month from the single training year of pairs gives X3 -0.049 (-0.089 to -0.007) against raw ENS and X4 +0.019 (-0.015 to +0.053) against the all-year stage 0, and the monthly ratios to CAMS stay between 0.82 and 1.12 (figure 1).

Stage 0 hurts one Primary series and rests on one training member and one year. Series P6 scores worse with stage 0 (+0.053, 0.037 to 0.073), and series P9, with 8 months of data, gains the most (-0.354). The training table held one ensemble member per run, the control member, so the mapping assumes the 50 perturbed members share its distribution. CAMS is held hourly while ENS shortwave is interpolated to half-hours, which the mapping ignores. The 14 months of pairs give April to June two years and the other months one. Validation is one year (2025-07 to 2026-06).

Scripts: ml-experiments/00014-cams-trained-stage1-with-stage0-ens-correction-demand/ (e00014_fit.py, e00014_post_hoc.py, e00014_score.py, e00014_charts.py).

docs.title: Does the same-time electricity price help a stage 1 demand model explain power?
docs.text:
We asked whether the electricity price at the same time as each demand reading helps a weather-to-power model explain demand. We added that price to the model and compared its error with the same model without it and with a control that used the price from a different week, on 17 series in a selection year and 18 in a confirmation year. The price lowered the error in the selection year, but the control gave most of the same gain, and the gain did not repeat in the confirmation year.

Verdict: inconclusive. The same-time price lowered the pooled error (the error averaged over all fitted series) in the selection year, but a price from another week reproduced most of that gain, and the gain did not repeat in the confirmation year. Follows experiment 00010, which tested the price from 7 days earlier at two battery sites and was inconclusive.

Absolute scores (mean absolute error of the median, points of capacity, 3 seeds, pooled over 17 fitted series in the selection year and 18 in the confirmation year):

Scope and year BASE PRICE SHUFFLED CONTROL CLIMATOLOGY Pooled, selection 9.86 9.34 9.41 9.35 12.38 Pooled, confirmation 9.11 8.93 8.99 8.50 12.36 B2, selection 10.98 9.88 9.77 10.08 15.46 B2, confirmation 10.12 10.13 10.09 9.23 15.01

docs.title: What the contrasts say
docs.text:
• C1 passed in the selection year only. −0.52 (−0.88 to −0.11), with 10 of 12 months below zero. In the confirmation year C1 is −0.18 (−0.50 to +0.08), with 6 of 12 months below zero.
  • C2 failed. The price against the other-week price is −0.07 (−0.17 to +0.03) in the selection year and −0.06 (−0.18 to +0.07) in the confirmation year, so the point estimate misses the −0.1 threshold and the interval includes zero. The other-week price carries the week's price level, and the point estimates say it matches 0.45 of the 0.52 points. That match has no interval of its own, and the C2 interval allows the share to lie between about 0.35 and 0.55 points, so the gain probably comes largely from any price column and not from the price at time t.
  • C3, price against national demand and wind: −0.01 (−0.39 to +0.41) in the selection year and +0.43 (−0.03 to +0.86) in the confirmation year. Both intervals include zero, so national demand and wind did no worse than the price. Only at B2 in the confirmation year does the interval exclude zero (+0.90, 0.55 to 1.21, in favour of national demand and wind).
  • C4, by hour (selection year): −0.27 (0 to 4), −0.56 (8 to 12), −0.78 (12 to 16), −0.83 (16 to 20), and −0.40 (20 to 24). In the confirmation year the gain is −0.30 (8 to 12), −0.38 (12 to 16), −0.31 (16 to 20), and +0.07 (20 to 24). The prediction that the gain peaks from 16:00 to 20:00 held in the selection year only. The predicted pooled gain of 0.1 to 0.3 points was exceeded in the selection year (0.52) and met in the confirmation year (0.18).
  • B2: −1.09 (−2.25 to −0.10) in the selection year, where the other-week price gave about the same (−1.20 against BASE). In the confirmation year B2 gained 0.00.
  • By series: in the selection year the price removes 0.11 to 0.19 of the squared residual at B1, B2, G1, G2, P2, and P6, and 0.05 or less at the other 11. Beside the other-week price it removes a further 0.06 or less at those six, so at most of them the price-level signal accounts for most of the gain. B2 is the exception: the other-week price gained 0.11 points more than the price did. Eight of the 11 other series get no gain at all, P15 (+0.79) and P8 (+0.26) the worst. At G1 the price lowers the error by 4.34 points, and by 0.54 points more than the other-week price does. In the confirmation year only P2 (0.21) and P6 (0.15) keep a gain, and P2 gains 1.04 points more than from the other-week price.

docs.title: Failures and deviations
docs.text:
• Some series have too little training history (17,520 half-hours before the purge), so 17 series were fitted in the selection year and 18 in the confirmation year, as in experiment 10.
  • The decision rule gives inconclusive: C1 and C2 did not both pass in the selection year, and the refuted branch needed the C1 interval wholly above −0.1 in both years, which it was not. The result is not a small gain by the skill's definition, because C2's interval includes zero.
  • The residual breakdowns do not give out-of-fold residuals over the whole history, which the later experiment needs.
  • No Opus review was run. Sonnet reviewed the plan and the code; the code review found no bug. The shuffled price is built over the whole history, so a training row within 4 weeks of the fold's end can carry a price from the purge or validation weeks. The shuffled column holds a price and no target, so no outcome leaks.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: The stage 1 demand model is a tool for a later experiment, not a forecaster. The model maps the observed price and weather at time t to power at time t. A later experiment could feed it the prices of the past to estimate the power that should have been metered, and so measure how unusual the actual lagged power was. That use needs two facts from this experiment: whether the price adds information beyond the weather and the clock, and in which hours and at which series it adds it. The ERA5 weather and the price at time t are both observed, so every score here is at observed values and none is a forecast skill.

docs.title: Design
docs.text:
The base is the experiment 00006 Primary input set: the weather block (ERA5 at the series' nearest grid cell), hour and weekday, the COVID indicator, and the days to Christmas inside a 14-day window, with recency weights (half-life 2 years). Folds, XGBoost settings (no column subsampling), purge, and the series fitted are those of experiment 10. A series needs 17,520 training half-hours before the purge to be fitted in a fold, so the count fitted is reported for each fold.

Arm Adds to BASE BASE nothing PRICE price_now: the APXMIDP price of the half-hour ending at valid_time; missing if the half-hour is missing or has zero volume SHUFFLED price_now taken from another week of the same weekday and half-hour, 1 to 4 weeks away in either direction, drawn with a fixed seed (a negative control) CONTROL GB national demand outturn (INDO) and wind output (FUELHH) at the same half-hour, the non-price national signals the price follows CLIMATOLOGY not a fit: the month-by-half-hour median of the fold's training window, as ClimatologyForecaster computes it

Weather and price source. The weather is ERA5, which arrives about 5 days late, so the stage 1 demand model cannot run at forecast time. The ERA5 dependence is intended, because the model scores past power. The price is the experiment 10 pull of APXMIDP, 98.5% complete and fully complete from 2024-04-14. Training rows before 2021 can have a missing price, which XGBoost handles natively.

Rows and row sets. All arms are scored on the same validation rows. A half-hour with a missing price is still predicted, because XGBoost treats the missing value natively. The climatology row drops a row whose calendar cell holds no training sample. The selection year's row set is era5_val_2024_07_to_2025_06_v1, and the confirmation year's is era5_val_2025_07_to_2026_06_v1.

Timing. The Elexon time column is the UTC start of the half-hour, and the join uses valid_time minus 30 minutes in UTC. The shuffled price moves a whole week at a time, so the shuffle can misalign a half-hour by one hour in the weeks that contain a clock change.

What a pass means. The price follows national demand and wind. A pass of C1 and C2 therefore shows that the price carries information beyond the weather and the clock, and C3 says whether it carries any beyond national demand and wind. Without C3 the price may only be a proxy for national conditions, so the write-up states C3 beside the verdict.

Calendar memorisation. BASE has hour and weekday, so the price column could stand in for the calendar. SHUFFLED keeps the price's calendar structure and removes its information, and C2 is the contrast that controls for it.

docs.title: Planned contrasts
docs.text:
All are differences in mean absolute error, in points of capacity, over the selection year (2024-07 to 2025-06) and then, once, the confirmation year (2025-07 to 2026-06), with a month-resampled interval, pooled over the fitted series and the 3 seeds.

  • C1 (verdict): PRICE − BASE.
  • C2 (verdict): PRICE − SHUFFLED.
  • C3 (descriptive): PRICE − CONTROL.
  • C4 (descriptive): C1 by local hour of day, in 4-hour blocks.

With 12 months, a month-resampled interval is close to the range of the monthly differences. The report therefore also prints the 12 paired monthly differences of C1 and C2 and the number of months with the sign the prediction gives, and the write-up reads the interval together with them.

Residual breakdowns, descriptive. For each local hour and each series, the report gives the mean absolute error of BASE and PRICE, and the share of BASE's squared residual that PRICE removes. The squared share is the number the later experiment needs. Beside each cell the report gives PRICE − SHUFFLED, the noise floor that a cell of this size shows with an uninformative price. The report uses absolute residuals as the headline and the squared share as a second view. The B2 gain is reported beside the pooled gain.

docs.title: Sizing
docs.text:
Sizing, one line per plan-issue trigger. Stores: private predictions only. Serving path: not touched. Degradation rule: not touched. More than one defensible design: yes (which price columns, which controls), fixed above. Code whose callers could not be named without searching: no, the code reuses experiment 10's. This is medium: one Sonnet plan review, one Sonnet code review, one Sonnet write-up review.

Limits. The later experiment needs out-of-fold residuals over the whole history. This experiment scores two validation years only, so it shows that the price helps and where, and it does not produce those residuals.

Resources. Slot B, 8 CPU cores, one thread per fit, no GPU.

Earlier advice. Follows experiment 10's advice to keep a shuffled-price control and a climatology row. Departs from its advice to test on series with large batteries, because the maintainer's design pools all series and reports B2 beside the pool.

docs.title: Does a correction bring the pooled mixture's 5% to 95% band to 90% coverage for solar and wind?
docs.text:
We asked whether a small correction can make the 5% to 95% band of a solar or wind forecast contain the measured output 90% of the time. That share is the band's coverage. We widened or narrowed the band by a factor, in several variants, and measured the coverage in five groups of lead times (0 to 24 hours, 1 to 2 days, and so on). For solar, one factor brought the share of outputs inside the band, which was 94% or 95%, down to about 90% in every group with no change in accuracy. For wind, no planned variant worked in the first two groups, and only a variant added after seeing the data did.

Verdict: partly supported. For solar, the planned spread factor brings the 5% to 95% band of the pooled mixture from 94% to 95% coverage to about 90% in every lead band, at no change in the CRPS. For wind, no planned arm brings the first two lead bands within 2.5 points of 90. A post hoc arm that pools the lead bands into two groups does. ENS is the ECMWF ensemble, ERA5 its reanalysis of past weather, CRPS the continuous ranked probability score, and stage 1a an XGBoost model per series trained on ERA5. The page is proposal P12 in the research plan, and the corrected pooled mixture of 00002's ERA5-trained stage 1a, with no new fit, is the input.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
• Uncorrected solar over-covers in every band. Coverage is 95.3%, 94.5%, 95.1%, 94.3%, and 94.7% from the first band to the last, against a target of 90%. The prediction said 2 to 3 points above 90 in at least one band, and the result is 4 to 5 points in all five.
  • Uncorrected wind over-covers in the first two days only. Coverage is 95.3%, 94.4%, 90.4%, 89.5%, and 90.1%, as predicted.
  • Solar: spread, spread_band, and free_quantile reach 90%. Every band lies within 2.5 points of 90 (for example spread at 91.8%, 89.9%, 91.4%, 89.5%, and 90.5%). The CRPS changes by +0.006 for spread (C2, 99.4% interval -0.004 to +0.024), +0.003 for spread_band (C4), and -0.011 for free_quantile (C8, -0.022 to +0.005). The fitted single factor is 0.90 to 1.00, median 0.95.
  • Wind: no planned arm reaches 90%. The closest planned arms in the first band are locscale (93.4%) and spread_band (94.7%), and in the second band spread_band (91.1%) and free_quantile (92.0%). The factor per band is 0.90 for both bands but exists in only 3 months (0 to 24 h) and 8 months (1 to 2 days), because the 5,000-case minimum is reached late. The single factor is 1.00 to 1.05 (C1 -0.002, C3 -0.010).
  • Wind: the location-and-scale arm undershoots 90% in the middle bands. Its coverage is 93.4%, 86.7%, 83.9%, 87.9%, and 88.6%, so it lies outside 2.5 points of 90 in the second and third bands and is further from 90 than no correction in the third to fifth bands. Its CRPS change is a separate result: C5 is -0.147 with an interval of -0.317 to +0.047.
  • Wind: the free quantile arm changes the CRPS by -0.181. The interval is -0.377 to +0.032 (C7), so it includes zero.
  • Prediction against result. The prediction that the spread factor per lead band and the location-and-scale arm bring every wind band within 2.5 points of 90 is wrong for both arms. The prediction that no arm changes the CRPS by more than 0.1 points is wrong for wind locscale and free_quantile (C5 and C7), although both intervals include zero.
  • Post hoc, wind: a spread factor on two lead groups reaches 90%. Coverage is 92.5%, 90.7%, 91.0%, 91.1%, and 91.5%, and the CRPS change is -0.021 (-0.042 to -0.002), a small gain: the interval excludes zero and the estimate is under the 0.05-point threshold of the decision rule. The arm was chosen after the planned results were seen, and the decision rule does not cover it.
  • Reference arms. The beta-transform blend of 00002 has the lowest wind CRPS (10.92, against 11.11 uncorrected) and 90.0% to 94.6% wind coverage. The stage 2 calibrator is worse than no correction on CRPS for both technologies (solar 5.43, wind 11.29).
  • Absolute CRPS (points of capacity, all leads): solar uncorrected 5.03, spread 5.03, locscale 5.04, climatology 5.63; wind uncorrected 11.11, spread 11.11, free_quantile 10.93, climatology 13.03. Seed spread is at most 0.002 for the arms listed.
  • Verdict. The decision rule gives one outcome per technology: supported for solar and refuted for wind. "Partly supported" names that split.

docs.title: Failures and limits
docs.text:
• The claims rest on 6 solar farms and 3 wind farms in one validation year. Farms of one technology differ: in 00002's scores wind farm coverage ranged from 88% to 95%, and a factor per technology cannot remove that.
  • The first month cannot be corrected, and the short wind bands stay uncorrected for most of the year. Over the months with a per-band fit, coverage for solar spread_band is 87.1% to 90.9%, and for wind spread_band is 93.3% in the first band and 89.0% in the second. The solar 0 to 24 h value is below the 2.5-point limit, so the solar result in that band is less firm than the all-months figures suggest.
  • The explanations for the wind result are untested. Too few cases for the per-band fit is consistent with the short fit history, but where the 0 to 24 h per-band fit exists its coverage is still 93.3%. No arm compared pooled and per-band fits over the same months.
  • The ENS validation year is the only year the stored mixture covers, so each correction is scored once and not selected on a second year.

docs.title: Lessons
docs.text:
• A single factor near 0.95 brought solar coverage within 2.5 points of 90 in every band with no detectable CRPS change. The upper bound of the CRPS interval is +0.024.
  • The location-and-scale calibrator per lead band was less reliable than a spread factor. Its CRPS interval is 0.36 points wide and its coverage undershoots 90% in two wind bands. Whether a larger sample would fix it is untested.
  • Pooling the lead bands into two groups reached 90% for wind in this sample. The arm was chosen after seeing the planned results, so a later experiment should test it on another year.

docs.title: Size
docs.text:
The size is complex, because the experiment adds new methods and admits more than one defensible design.

  • What gets stored: private predictions only. No schema in packages/contracts/ changes.
  • Production serving path: not touched. The calibrators run on stored quantiles after the fact.
  • Degradation rule: not touched.
  • More than one defensible design: yes. The correction can scale about the median or about each quantile, and can be fitted globally or per lead band.
  • Code whose callers cannot be named without searching: no. The mixture arithmetic copies studies/stage1_pilot/stage2_common.py, and the stored member quantiles are experiment 00002's.

docs.title: Which earlier advice the plan followed
docs.text:
• Followed: pool the ERA5-trained quantiles over the ECMWF ensemble (ENS) members before any calibrator (00002); report the pooled mixture beside every calibrated arm (00002); fit the correction on earlier validation months only, as 00002's beta-transform blend does.
  • Departs from: nothing. No arm uses lagged power, so the advice on lagged power does not apply.
  • Not tested: the PV ratio target and the wind base_margin that the research plan lists for this proposal. Experiment 00012 found the two within 0.05 points of its benchmark (C3, C4), and both change stage 1a and not its calibration.

docs.title: Setup
docs.text:
Rows and series. The 6 solar farms (labels A to F) and 3 wind farms (W1 to W3) of fold_a_tuesdays_v1: 53 runs on Tuesdays, valid times from 2025-07-01 to 2026-06-30, every valid time with an observed power. Labels are anonymised in the write-up.

Inputs. Stage 1a is an XGBoost model per series, trained on ERA5 weather and fitted before 2025-06-17, so every validation case is out of sample. The stage 2 calibrator of 00002 is not used here. The 9 quantile levels (5%, 10%, 25%, 40%, 50%, 60%, 75%, 90%, 95%) of each of the 51 ENS members, from the ERA5-trained stage 1a of experiment 00002 (full variant), pooled into a mixture as in 00002 separately for each fitting seed (0, 1, 2); each seed is corrected and scored on its own. ERA5 is used only in training, so no past weather enters at forecast time, and no arm uses a lag or a calendar column.

Fitting the corrections. The cases of a scored month are the runs whose initialisation time falls in that month. Each arm is fitted per technology on the cases with valid times before the first run of the scored month, so that a fit sees no outcome later than the earliest forecast it is applied to. A fit uses only non-trivial cases, those whose uncorrected 95% quantile exceeds 1% of capacity, and trivial cases (night-time solar zeros) are left uncorrected. A fit needs at least 5,000 earlier non-trivial cases (per lead band for the band arms); with fewer the arm returns the uncorrected mixture, so the first months of the year, which cannot be fitted, are scored uncorrected. The write-up states which months and bands this affects, gives the number of earlier runs beside each fit's case count (one run supplies a few hundred cases that share one weather situation), and reports coverage over the corrected months alone as well as over all months.

docs.title: Arms
docs.text:
Arm Correction of the mixture's quantiles q and median m none None spread m + k (q - m), one k per technology, the value on a grid of 0.60 to 1.60 in steps of 0.05 whose coverage is nearest 90% spread_band The same, with one k per technology and lead band locscale m + a + k (q - m), one (a, k) per technology and lead band, minimising the mean CRPS on a grid (a from -0.05 to +0.05 in steps of 0.01, k as above) free_quantile q_t + d_t, where d_t is the t-quantile of the observed power minus q_t over the fitted cases, per technology, lead band, and level

The locscale fit draws at most 30,000 of the fitting cases, at random with a fixed seed, to limit the cost of its grid search. Each corrected quantile is clipped to 0 to 1 of capacity and the nine are then sorted.

docs.title: Planned contrasts
docs.text:
Each is the arm's CRPS minus that of none, in points of capacity, per technology, over all leads (the lead-band tables are descriptive).

Id Technology Arm C1, C2 wind, solar spread C3, C4 wind, solar spread_band C5, C6 wind, solar locscale C7, C8 wind, solar free_quantile

docs.title: Checks before the contrasts are read
docs.text:
• Reproduction. none, averaged over the three seeds, must reproduce 00002's b_mixture_full mean CRPS to within 0.05 points per technology (11.11 for wind and 5.05 for solar), or the experiment stops.
  • Leakage review. A reviewer reads the code to confirm that no fit reads a case whose valid time is not before the first run of the scored month.

docs.title: Post hoc arm
docs.text: spread_two_groups (script e00016_posthoc.py) fits one spread factor per technology and lead group (0 to 2 days, 3 to 15 days) by the spread rule. It is outside the pre-registered contrasts, and its CRPS contrasts H1 and H2 are descriptive.

docs.title: Resolution limit
docs.text: The data are 9 series in two weather regions and one validation year. The write-up reads coverage differences of a few percentage points per technology and descriptively, and shows coverage with a month-resampled 95% interval.

docs.title: Experiment 17: training window, recency, and retraining rule for demand
docs.text:
We asked whether a demand model forecasts better when it is trained only on recent data, retrained often, or corrected using its recent errors. We tested these rules on 16 Primary substations (substations that step power down to the local distribution network), with monthly forecasts from January 2022 to June 2026. Every rule that follows recent data beat training on all history, and a correction using the previous 14 days of errors beat all of them. The tests used estimates of past weather in place of weather forecasts, so the scores are a ceiling on what these rules would reach with weather available at forecast time.

Supported: every rule that follows recent data beat all history, and the 14-day correction beat all of them. Scores are the mean absolute error of the median in points of capacity (1 point is 1% of a series' effective capacity), on 16 Primary substations, with monthly forecasts from January 2022 to June 2026 (1.07 million half-hours). Weather is ERA5 (a reanalysis, an estimate of past weather), which arrives about 5 days late, so the scores are a ceiling on what forecast-time weather reaches. The fitting code is in ml-experiments/00017-*/; the sliding windows are 183, 365, and 548 days. The mean absolute error of the median is the average gap between the median forecast and the measured power.

Arm Error (95% interval) Against A (99.44% interval) A: all history, monthly retrain 7.62 (7.28 to 7.98) reference W6: 6-month window 7.32 (6.97 to 7.70) -0.30 (-0.91 to +0.32) W12: 12-month window 6.77 (6.48 to 7.11) -0.84 (-1.19 to -0.53) W18: 18-month window 6.82 (6.52 to 7.17) -0.79 (-1.15 to -0.48) H0.5: half-life 0.5 years 6.70 (6.42 to 7.00) -0.92 (-1.22 to -0.64) H1: half-life 1 year 6.91 (6.63 to 7.23) -0.71 (-0.92 to -0.51) H2: half-life 2 years 7.16 (6.86 to 7.50) -0.45 (-0.57 to -0.34) F: never retrained 11.42 (10.86 to 12.02) +3.80 (+3.12 to +4.47) Y: retrained yearly 8.14 (7.76 to 8.54) +0.52 (+0.30 to +0.81) K: A plus 14-day correction 6.10 (5.88 to 6.32) -1.52 (-1.95 to -1.13) Month-by-half-hour climatology 8.44 (8.02 to 8.88) not paired

The drift reverses sign, and that is why recent rows win. A's mean error (observed minus forecast) runs from about -3.8 points in 2022 and 2023 (forecast too high) to +1.8 in the first half of 2026 (forecast too low). In 2026 the 12-month window and the half-lives overshoot to +3.0 to +3.4, yet still score 8.3 to 8.6 against A's 9.4. Only the 6-month window and the correction stay near zero, the correction within 0.2 points in every year (figure 2).

Three predictions missed, and one held with a larger size. The recency and correction gains were 0.5 to 1.5 points, against the 0.1 to 0.3 predicted. The 6-month window lowered the error by 0.3 points where a rise was predicted, though its interval straddles zero. The frozen XGBoost model raised the error by 3.8 points, which meets the predicted rise of at least 0.5 and exceeds it.

Failures and limits. No fit failed. The correction needs observed power 2 days old, so it is only as good as the live telemetry delay. All scores use ERA5 weather.

docs.title: Post hoc contrasts
docs.text: The correction stacks with shorter memory. The correction applied to H0.5 scores 5.82 (95% interval 5.63 to 6.02), 0.27 points (0.21 to 0.34) below the correction on A. Applied to W12, it scores 5.84. These contrasts were not pre-registered.

docs.title: Does the staged chain beat the single-stage model for Primary substation demand?
docs.text:
We asked whether a chain of two forecasting stages beats a single-step model for demand at Primary substations (substations that step power down to the local distribution network), when both use only the data a live service would have, including the real delay in NGED's power readings. We scored the chain, the single-step model, and a simple baseline on the same 73 forecast runs. The chain scored 0.08 points of capacity worse than the single-step model and 0.52 worse than the baseline, and neither difference was clear of zero, so the chain is not supported for demand.

Verdict: inconclusive. With lag anomalies built only from weather that would be available at forecast time, and with NGED's real telemetry delay, the quantile score of the staged chain (an ERA5-trained stage 1 followed by a stage 2 calibrator that also reads recent power, as lag anomalies and stage 1 residuals) is not distinguishable from N1's: 6.41 against 6.33, and C1 is +0.08 points of capacity (99.17% interval -0.11 to +0.25). The chain's point estimate is above manual_heuristic's 5.89 by +0.52 (-0.25 to +1.25, C3). Neither interval excludes zero. The decision rule needed both to be wholly below zero by at least 0.3, so the staged design is not supported for demand on this evidence. The prediction, that the chain would score 0.3 to 0.8 below N1, was missed. A point is 1% of the series' effective capacity. The substations are not named. N1 is the single-stage XGBoost quantile model trained on the ensemble weather forecast (ENS) of the European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts. manual_heuristic is a stored baseline that forecasts from the power at the same time of day in earlier weeks and years.

docs.title: What the arms score
docs.text:
Every arm is scored on the same 768,073 cases per seed (Primary substations; 965,723 for all 20 series), on the 73 runs of fold_a_every5d_v1. Intervals resample whole months and the three seeds. Quantile score (an estimate of the continuous ranked probability score), smaller is better:

Arm All leads Up to 48 h 3 days or more Median error, all leads Bias Coverage manual_heuristic 5.89 5.68 5.94 8.23 -1.34 80.9% N1 6.33 5.59 6.51 8.45 -2.60 80.1% Chain, final ERA5 lag anomalies (ceiling) 6.28 5.32 6.50 8.47 -1.99 86.2% Chain, serving-latency lag anomalies (S) 6.41 5.32 6.66 8.64 -2.12 86.1% Chain, S with a spread factor of 1.15 6.37 5.31 6.61 8.64 -2.12 90.0% Chain, raw lagged power only 6.46 5.45 6.70 8.64 -2.22 86.3% Chain, S at 3.5 hours of delay 6.28 5.16 6.54 8.52 -2.30 86.3% Stage 1 and calibrator, no lagged power (R0c) 7.46 7.11 7.56 10.02 -3.45 85.8% climatology 7.46 7.39 7.49 10.33 -2.87 83.0% Production recipe 9.52 9.38 9.58 9.92 -2.28 9.7%

Bias is the mean of the median forecast minus the observed power, in points of capacity. Coverage is the share of observations inside the 5% to 95% band.

docs.title: The six planned contrasts
docs.text:
Quantile score, Primary substations, 99.17% intervals; negative means the first arm is better.

  • C1 (primary), chain minus N1: +0.08 over all leads (-0.11 to +0.25), -0.27 up to 48 h (-0.62 to +0.03), +0.15 beyond 3 days (-0.07 to +0.36).
  • C2, chain minus R0c: -1.05 over all leads (-1.64 to -0.58), -1.79 up to 48 h. Experiment 00005 measured -1.80 over leads up to 48 hours with final ERA5 and no delay.
  • C3, chain minus manual_heuristic: +0.52 (-0.25 to +1.25), -0.36 up to 48 h (-0.89 to +0.12), +0.72 beyond 3 days (-0.14 to +1.54).
  • C4, chain minus the final-ERA5 ceiling: +0.13 (+0.02 to +0.25), so serving sources lose 0.13.
  • C5, chain minus raw lagged power only: -0.04 (-0.12 to +0.07), -0.14 up to 48 h (-0.30 to -0.03). Lag anomalies add little to the lags themselves.
  • C6, spread factor minus no factor: -0.04 (-0.08 to -0.00). The factor k was 1.15, chosen on calibration rows only, and lifts the coverage from 86.1% to 90.0%.

docs.title: Exploratory contrasts (95% intervals)
docs.text:
• The CAMS swap and the proxy change the score by 0.01 or less. The chain with and without CAMS shortwave differ by +0.01 over all leads (E1, 0.00 to +0.01) and by +0.01 up to 48 h (+0.01 to +0.03), so the swap is a tiny worsening. The proxy alone against the serving mix differs by 0.00 (E2).
  • Telemetry delay matters up to 48 hours. The chain with final ERA5 and the 7-hour delay scores 0.05 better than with a 0.5-hour delay over all leads (E3, -0.17 to +0.05), but 0.11 worse up to 48 h. With 3.5 hours of delay, as N1 had, the chain beats N1 up to 48 h by 0.43 (-0.72 to -0.15, E5) and is level with it over all leads (-0.04, -0.18 to +0.07). The extra 3.5 hours cost 0.13 (E7).
  • The production recipe is far behind. The chain beats it by 3.11 (E4).

docs.title: Limits
docs.text:
• ERA5T is emulated by final ERA5, and the CAMS values are the real history rather than the value available on the day, so C4 may understate the cost of serving latency.
  • One calibrator and spread factor per substation type; N1 has no calibration, so its 80% coverage is part of its score.
  • Calibration residuals are at most 3 months from a model's fit, while validation residuals come from a final model up to 12 months old. The page did not measure the residual scale by months since fit.
  • 16 series and 12 months leave 99.17% intervals of about plus or minus 0.2 for the paired contrasts and plus or minus 0.8 against manual_heuristic.
  • Every arm under-forecast the validation year by 1.3 to 3.5 points (the bias column), so the scores above mix bias with the other error.
  • The review used Sonnet, not Opus, because the maintainer asked for Opus only where vital.

docs.title: Lessons learned
docs.text:
• The staged design is not supported for demand on this evidence. The chain is not distinguishable from N1, and its point estimate is above manual_heuristic's. Its point estimates are lower only up to 2 days, with intervals that include zero.
  • Raw lagged power carries most of the lag signal. Lag anomalies add 0.04 over all leads.
  • Telemetry delay and weather source matter at different leads. Delay matters up to 48 hours (E7 +0.16, C4 0.00), and the weather source beyond 3 days (C4 +0.16, E7 +0.12).
  • A spread factor helps. Coverage rose from 86% to 90% and the quantile score fell by 0.04.

docs.title: Plan, written before any code ran
Plan: sizing
docs.text:
• Stored data: prediction sets under data/ml-experiments/; no production table changes.
  • Production serving path: not touched.
  • Degradation rule: not touched.
  • Defensible designs: more than one. The weather source at each lag time, the telemetry delay, and the spread factor each have more than one defensible form; each is fixed below before a fit.
  • Callers: the scripts copy the helpers of experiments 00005 and 00013, which the author of this plan could name without searching.

Size: complex. The plan gets one Sonnet review, the code gets two Sonnet reviews (leakage and the fit stopping at the fold's end; then correctness), and the write-up gets one. Opus is not used, because the maintainer asked for Opus only where vital.

docs.title: Plan: what differs from experiment 00005
docs.text:
Experiment 00005 measured the lag gain with a ceiling, because the lag anomaly (observed power at a lag time minus stage 1's expectation at that time) used final ERA5 weather at past times and a forecast origin with no telemetry delay. This experiment changes three inputs and nothing else in the chain.

  • Telemetry delay. NGED's files cover 6-hour windows ending at 02:00, 08:00, 14:00, and 20:00 UTC, and in this project's downloaded-files list each file lands 3.0 hours after its window ends (median over the 26,697 files from 2026-03-26). The forecast origin is 09:00 UTC, 9 hours after the 00:00 UTC ENS run. The newest observed half-hour usable at the origin is therefore the one ending 02:00 UTC, 7 hours before the origin. Experiment 00013 assumed 3.5 hours. A lag is usable only when its time is at or before that newest half-hour.
  • Weather at lag times. Stage 1's expectation at a lag time uses one of four weather sources, all emulated from data on disk, and every source respects what serving has at 09:00 UTC. ERA5T is emulated by final ERA5 and is available for times at least 5 days before the origin. CAMS irradiance (hourly, at the series' location) is available up to 00:00 UTC of the origin day. The analysis proxy is the ENS control member of the freshest run that had started by the lag time (lead 0 to 24 hours, so a run's first day), as weather_utils.analysis_proxy defines it, and is available to the origin. ERA5T differs slightly from final ERA5, and the emulation ignores that.
  • Lag times. The anomalies and residuals use the times 24, 48, 168, and 336 hours before the valid time, the newest usable half-hour and the ones 1 and 3 hours before it, and the latest earlier time with the valid time's half-hour of day and of week. A lag is null when its time is after the newest usable half-hour (origin minus 7 hours), so the 24-hour lag is unusable at leads up to 17 hours.
  • Which stage 1 models. Calibration origins use the forward-chain stage 1 model of their quarter, and validation origins use the final model, both from experiment 00005. A chain model stops 15 days before its quarter starts, and an origin reads lag times no earlier than 14 days before itself, so every expectation is out of sample. The experiment refits nothing in stage 1.

docs.title: Plan: arms
docs.text:
All arms use stage 1a from experiment 00005 (from2023: ERA5-trained from 2023-09, 13 columns) the same ENS statistics (mean, standard deviation, 10th, 50th, and 90th percentile of the 51 members, plus the lead), and the same stage 2 calibrator (multi-quantile XGBoost, depth 4, 300 rounds, 9 levels, per series, trained on every third daily run from 2024-04-01 to 2025-06-30). They differ only in the recent-origin inputs. Seeds are 0, 1, and 2.

  • CH-none: raw recent power only: the newest usable power, the power 1 and 3 hours before it, the power at the same time of day and of week, and the four power lags (24, 48, 168, and 336 hours), no lag anomalies.
  • CH-S (serving): the same inputs plus the stage 1 residuals and lag anomalies. A lag time at least 5 days before the origin takes ERA5T. A later one up to 00:00 UTC of the origin day takes the analysis proxy with its shortwave replaced by CAMS. A later one still takes the analysis proxy. This is the arm whose contrasts decide the verdict.
  • CH-S-noCAMS: as CH-S, without the CAMS swap.
  • CH-P (proxy): the analysis proxy at every lag time.
  • CH-E (ceiling, real delay): final ERA5 at every lag time, with the 7-hour delay.
  • CH-S-delay3.5: as CH-S with the 3.5-hour delay that experiment 00013 gave N1 and manual_heuristic, so C1 and C3 can be read at equal telemetry freshness. It is exploratory.
  • CH-E-nodelay (replicates 00005's L3): final ERA5 and a 0.5-hour delay, as 00005 had.
  • CH-S-spread: CH-S quantiles with the spread scaled about the median, q50 + k (q - q50), by one factor k for the Primary substations (and one each for the bulk and grid supply points). k is chosen from the grid 1.00 to 1.60 in steps of 0.05 on held-out calibration rows: a calibrator fitted on the calibration runs before 2025-01-01 scored on the runs from 2025-01-01 to 2025-06-30 by quantile score. The scored arm uses the full-window calibrator and that k. No validation row influences k. N1 gets no equivalent tuning, so C6 is descriptive and the verdict never rests on it.
  • References from stored predictions: N1 (00013), manual_heuristic, climatology, and the production recipe (00013), and R0c, the lag-free calibrated stage 1 (00005), each repeated once per seed where unseeded.

docs.title: Plan: planned contrasts
docs.text:
Quantile score over all leads and by lead band, on the 16 Primary substations, 99.17% intervals.

  • C1 (primary): CH-S minus N1.
  • C2: CH-S minus R0c (the lag-free calibrated stage 1; 00005 measured -1.80 with ERA5 and no delay).
  • C3: CH-S minus manual_heuristic.
  • C4: CH-S minus CH-E (what the serving sources cost against final ERA5 at the same delay).
  • C5: CH-S minus CH-none (what lag anomalies add to raw lagged power).
  • C6: CH-S-spread minus CH-S, on the quantile score; coverage is read beside it.

Exploratory (95%): CH-S minus CH-S-noCAMS, CH-S minus CH-P, CH-E minus CH-E-nodelay (the cost of the real telemetry delay), CH-S minus the production recipe, and the same contrasts for the two bulk supply points and the two grid supply points, which are descriptive.

docs.title: Plan: bias
docs.text: Every arm in experiment 00013 under-forecast the validation year by 1.3 to 3.1 points. The page reports the mean signed error of the median for every arm and lead band, and the mean absolute error after subtracting each arm's per-series mean signed error (an oracle on the validation year, labelled post hoc), so the drift is not mistaken for a difference between arms.

docs.title: Plan: design confounds
docs.text:
• Training data differs by design. Stage 1 trains on ERA5 from 2023-09, which predates the ENS archive that N1 trains on (from 2024-04). That difference is part of the staged design under test, not a defect.
  • Column choice. Experiment 00006 chose stage 1's 13 columns on its own selection year (2024-07 to 2025-06), before any 2025-07 data was scored.
  • Residual scale. Calibration residuals come from models at most 3 months past their fit, and validation residuals from a final model up to 12 months past its fit. The write-up reports the residual scale by months since fit.

docs.title: Plan: leakage and cleanliness
docs.text:
• Nothing is scored on or after 2026-07-01.
  • Lag times, ERA5, CAMS, and proxy rows are all at or before the newest usable half-hour, which is at or before the origin minus 7 hours; a unit check asserts this on every case, and also each source's cutoff: ERA5T times at least 5 days before the origin, CAMS times up to 00:00 UTC of the origin day, and proxy values from a run started by the lag time.
  • Stage 1 models are never refitted. The calibrator trains on valid times up to 2025-06-30 23:30.
  • The spread factor k uses calibration runs only.
  • No calendar column enters the calibrator, as in 00005.

docs.title: Plan: ceiling labels and caveats
docs.text:
• CAMS irradiance enters an ERA5-trained stage 1 as shortwave; the two products differ in bias and scale, so the CH-S-noCAMS contrast shows whether the swap helps.
  • The ENS archive starts on 2024-04-01, so calibration origins in the first 5 days have null proxy-window lags.
  • ERA5T is emulated by final ERA5.

docs.title: Not tested here
docs.text: Solar and wind series, a second fold, other weather models, and a recency-weighted stage 1.

docs.title: Experiment 19: does stacking small gains beat manual_heuristic for Primary demand?
docs.text:
We asked whether stacking several small improvements gives a demand forecast for Primary substations (substations that step power down to the local distribution network) that beats a stored baseline built from the power at the same time in earlier weeks. The stack added to a single-step model a correction using the previous 14 days of forecast errors, a weighting of recent years, and a 15% widening of the forecast range. We scored it on 16 Primary substations over 73 forecast runs from July 2025 to June 2026. The stack beat the baseline and the single-step model, and the 14-day correction supplied nearly all of the gain.

Supported: the full stack beats manual_heuristic and N1, and the 14-day error correction supplies nearly all of the gain (-0.99 of -1.00). N1 is the single-stage quantile model trained on the control member of the ensemble weather forecast (ENS) of the European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts. Scores are the quantile score over all leads, in points of capacity (1 point is 1% of a series' effective capacity), on 16 Primary substations, 73 forecast runs every 5 days from July 2025 to June 2026, with ENS weather. C1, the stack minus manual_heuristic, is -0.56 (99.44% interval -0.93 to -0.26), and the mean absolute error of the median agrees (-0.88, -1.51 to -0.30). C2, the stack minus N1, is -1.00 (-1.88 to -0.14), which meets the -0.3 threshold. The stack's quantile score is 5.32, N1's is 6.33, and manual_heuristic's is 5.89. Up to 48 hours the stack scores 4.61 against 5.68 (C1, 95% interval -1.38 to -0.79), and from 3 days on 5.49 against 5.94. The quantile score measures how well the forecast quantiles fit what happened, and smaller is better. manual_heuristic is a stored baseline that forecasts from the power at the same time of day in earlier weeks and years.

Arm Quantile score Median error 5%-95% band covers 10%-90% band covers manual_heuristic 5.89 8.23 81% 72% climatology 7.46 10.33 83% 74% Production recipe 9.52 9.92 10% 8% N1 6.33 8.45 80% 71% N1 plus correction 5.34 7.34 80% 70% N1 with half-life 0.5 years 6.34 8.46 80% 70% N1 plus spread factor 6.28 8.45 85% 77% Full stack 5.32 7.35 85% 76% Stack without correction 6.29 8.46 85% 77% Stack without half-life 5.32 7.34 85% 76% Stack without spread factor 5.35 7.35 80% 70%

The correction removes a level bias. N1, frozen at 2025-06-30, forecast the validation year 2.6 points too low on average. The correction cuts that bias to 0.5, and the median error falls by 1.1 points (C7: -0.99 on the quantile score, -1.84 to -0.15 at 99.44%, 7 of 12 months below zero). Dropping the correction from the stack raises the score by 0.97 (C4, +0.15 to +1.81). The half-life does nothing here. C8 is +0.01 (-0.01 to +0.05) and C5 is -0.005 (-0.026 to +0.016), so the 0.5-year half-life earns no place. The spread factor is worth a small gain. C9 is -0.05 (-0.09 to -0.01), and dropping the factor raises the stack's score by 0.026 (C6, +0.005 to +0.049, threshold zero), though 5% to 95% coverage is only 85%.

The singles add up to the stack's gain. The three single gains sum to -1.02 (C7 -0.99, C8 +0.01, C9 -0.05) against the stack's -1.00 (C2), so the components overlap by at most 0.02 points.

The stack's gains fall in the predicted ranges, except the correction's, which is larger. The stack's gain over N1 (-1.00) falls in the predicted -0.6 to -1.2, and over manual_heuristic (-0.56) in -0.2 to -0.8. The correction's gain (-0.99) is larger than the predicted drop of 0.4 to 0.9, the half-life's (+0.01) is inside its range, and the spread factor's (-0.05) is at the top of its range. C1's interval is narrower than the plus or minus 0.7 predicted.

docs.title: Limits
docs.text:
• The correction's history comes from 5-day-spaced runs. A past half-hour's forecast has a lead of 0 to 5 days, so the history errors are larger than a daily service would see, and the correction is applied at every lead to 15 days. A daily service would use leads under 1 day.
  • N1 is never retrained. The correction partly stands in for monthly retraining, which experiment 00017 found lowers the error by 0.5 points (retrained monthly against yearly); the two have not been combined.
  • The production row's coverage of 10% is a property of the stored forecast, not of this experiment. Its stored quantiles come from ensemble members and are not a calibrated band.
  • The half-life was chosen on the scored year, and 26 of 1,460 series-runs (73 runs times 20 series; the first runs of some series) had no history and received a correction of zero.
  • The 3.5-hour telemetry delay is assumed, as in experiment 00013.

docs.title: Plan, written before any code ran
Plan: sizing
docs.text:
• Stored data: prediction sets only, under data/ml-experiments/.
  • Production serving path: not touched.
  • Degradation rule: not touched.
  • Defensible designs: more than one; the correction's history source and window, and the half-life, are fixed below before any fit.
  • Callers: the scripts copy 00013's helpers and read its stored predictions, which the author could name without searching.

Size: complex, because more than one defensible design tests the hypothesis. One Sonnet review of the plan, one of the code (leakage, fit stopping at the training end), and one of the write-up (Opus is kept for work that is truly vital).

docs.title: Plan: arms
docs.text:
Rows, series, columns, lags, seeds (0, 1, 2), and pooling over the 51 members are those of experiment 00013 (73 runs of fold_a_every5d_v1, valid times before 2026-07-01).

  • Stored: manual_heuristic, climatology, the production recipe, and N1, read from 00013.
  • N1H: N1 refitted with a recency half-life of 0.5 years in place of 2 years, anchored at 2025-06-30. Nothing else changes. The model is frozen at that date, as N1 is.
  • Correction (C): for each series and run with origin T, the mean of (observed power minus the median forecast) over the half-hours in the 14 days ending at the newest usable observation (00013's telemetry assumption: 3.5 hours before T), added to every quantile. The forecast for a past half-hour comes from the validation run with the latest origin at or before that half-hour, so only earlier runs are used. A run with fewer than 3 days of scored history gets no correction. The runs are 5 days apart, so a past forecast has a lead of 0 to 5 days; a daily service would use leads under 1 day, and the error of the correction on these rows is probably larger than the service's.
  • Spread (S): each quantile q becomes q50 + 1.15 * (q - q50), with q50 the corrected median where the correction applies. The factor is 00018's, fitted on the staged chain, not on N1.
  • Arms by component: N1, N1+C, N1+H, N1+S, the full stack F = H+C+S, and the three drops F-C (H+S), F-H (N1+C+S), F-S (H+C).

docs.title: Plan: leakage checks
docs.text: The scoring script asserts that every observation entering a correction has a grid index at or before the origin minus 7 half-hours, that the run supplying the forecast for a past half-hour has an origin at or before that half-hour, that a run with fewer than 3 days of history gets a correction of zero (and reports how many rows that is), and that N1H's training rows end at 2025-06-30 23:30. Observed power is read through load_series_arrays, as in 00013, and the median is the pooled mixture's q50. The spread factor is not re-tuned on N1; the 5% to 95% coverage of every arm is reported.

docs.title: Plan: limits stated in advance
docs.text:
• The half-life was chosen on the scored year. 00017 chose 0.5 years on origins through June 2026, which overlap this validation year, and 00017 retrained monthly. N1H is frozen and trained on 15 months, so its weights fall to about a quarter at the start of the archive.
  • The correction's history has leads of 0 to 5 days (runs are 5 days apart) and is applied to leads up to 15 days, and N1 already carries origin lags, so 00017's 1.5-point gain, measured on a model with no power lags, may not transfer.

docs.title: Plan: past weather
docs.text: ENS weather in training and scoring; lags and the correction use observed power before the origin. No past weather is used.

docs.title: Plan: earlier advice
docs.text: Followed: compare against manual_heuristic on both metrics (00013, 00018); test a deployable recent-error correction (00013, 00017); the 0.5-year half-life (00017); the 1.15 spread factor (00018). Departure: N1 is not retrained monthly, so the half-life is tested without 00017's moving anchor.

docs.title: Do the candidate changes for solar and wind add up to a better pooled mixture?
docs.text:
We asked whether combining the small improvements found earlier for solar and wind farm forecasts gives a better forecast than the current method. We built the full combination, removed each improvement in turn, and measured the accuracy of the forecast range. For wind, the combination improved accuracy by 0.071 points of capacity, and a starting guess taken from the turbine power curve supplied most of it. For solar, no improvement helped detectably.

Verdict: partly supported. For wind, the full stack (a power-curve base margin and a spread factor) lowers the continuous ranked probability score (CRPS) by 0.071 points of capacity, and the base margin carries the gain. For solar, no component detectably helped and the full stack was 0.035 points higher, with an interval that does not rule out a gain of 0.075. ENS is the European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts ensemble, ERA5 its reanalysis of past weather, and CAMS the Copernicus Atmosphere Monitoring Service's satellite irradiance estimate. The production recipe (arm base) is the pooled ERA5-trained mixture of experiment 00002. This is proposal P22 of the research plan. This experiment combines the changes that experiment 00012, experiment 00014, and experiment 00016 flagged as candidates or small gains, and drops each in turn. Gains of this size may not add, because the CAMS-trained stage 1a XGBoost model and the stage 0 mapping act on the same ENS irradiance bias.

docs.title: Size
docs.text:
• What gets stored: private prediction sets and tables only. No schema in packages/contracts/ changes.
  • Production serving path: not touched.
  • Degradation rule: not touched.
  • More than one defensible design: yes. The stage 0 form (a regression, as in 00012, or a quantile mapping, as in 00014), the spread-factor grouping, and the form of the wind base margin for a multi-quantile objective all admit alternatives. This page fixes one of each.
  • Code whose callers cannot be named without searching: no. The scripts copy the patterns of experiments 00012, 00014, and 00016, which an experiment may not import.

The size is complex, so the plan, the code, and the write-up each get a Sonnet review.

docs.title: Which earlier advice this plan follows
docs.text:
• Followed: keep the training start at 2019-09 and leave out the clear-sky-ratio target (00012); pair a CAMS-trained stage 1a with a stage 0 mapping onto the same irradiance and check the member spread afterwards (00014); scale the solar mixture's quantiles by one factor, and the wind mixture's on two lead groups (under 72 h, and 72 h or more), refitted monthly on earlier cases (00016); report absolute scores and the climatology beside every contrast (00001).
  • Departs from: 00012's stage 0 was a regression on the control member, which gave no gain on the member average. This plan uses 00014's empirical quantile mapping, which kept the member spread. Fitting stage 0 on the whole ensemble is not possible, because the ENS training table holds member 0 only.

docs.title: Design
docs.text:
Rows and series. The 6 solar farms and 3 wind farms of fold_a_tuesdays_v1: 53 runs on Tuesdays with valid times from 2025-07-01 to 2026-06-30, three seeds. Only labels appear in the write-up.

Stage 1a quantile model. One XGBoost model per series and seed with the 9-level multi-quantile objective of experiment 00002 (500 rounds, eta 0.05, depth 6), the same columns as 00001 (9 for solar, 6 for wind), no calendar and no power-lag column, trained on cleaned power at valid times from 2019-09 to before 2025-06-17. The pooled mixture treats the 51 members' 9 quantiles as equal-weight atoms, as in 00002.

Weather source at forecast time. ENS members only. ERA5 and CAMS are read at training only, so nothing needs to exist at forecast time that is late (ERA5 arrives about 5 days late). No arm has a lag column.

Fit windows. Every fit uses cleaned power and ERA5 or CAMS weather at valid times before 2025-06-17: the stage 1a quantile models, the wind power curve (refitted for each seed on the series' own training rows), and the stage 0 mappings. Training reads the ERA5 100 m wind speed and forecasting reads the ENS speed, which the base margin inherits. A margin makes XGBoost ignore its base score, and the same margin goes to all 9 levels, so the predicted quantiles are sorted afterwards. The code guards that the margin changes the predictions.

Spread factor. Each arm refits its own factor on its own earlier cases (a factor from experiment 00016 would not fit different quantiles). A fit needs at least 5,000 non-trivial earlier cases (cases whose uncorrected 95% quantile exceeds 1% of capacity); a month or lead group without a fit stays uncorrected. The first month never has earlier cases, and the short wind lead groups fit late in the year, which bounds what any spread-factor contrast can show. The two wind lead groups were chosen after experiment 00016's results and are validated here on the same year.

Stage 0 checks (descriptive). The write-up reports, for each solar arm with a stage 0 mapping, the ratio of the mapped ENS daylight shortwave to the target irradiance by month, and the member spread before and after, as experiment 00014 did.

Components.

Component Technology What it changes CAMS-trained solar The shortwave column of training rows is CAMS irradiance at the farm, not ERA5 shortwave Stage 0 solar An empirical quantile mapping per lead band and zenith bin (00014's design) maps each ENS member's shortwave onto the irradiance the stage 1a trained on, CAMS for a CAMS-trained arm and ERA5 for an ERA5-trained arm. The mapping is fitted on the control member's pairs with valid times before 2025-06-17, pooled over the 6 farms (the run asserts the latest valid time) Base margin wind The 100 m wind-speed power curve (binned mean power, running maximum) is the booster's base margin for all 9 quantiles Spread factor both The quantiles are scaled about the median by the factor nearest 90% coverage of the 5% to 95% band, fitted for each scored month on non-trivial cases with valid times before the first run of that month. Solar uses one factor, wind one for leads under 72 h (the first two lead bands) and one for longer leads

Arms.

Arm Solar Wind base ERA5-trained, raw ENS ERA5-trained, raw ENS cams CAMS-trained n/a cams_s0 CAMS-trained, stage 0 n/a margin n/a base margin base_spread base + spread factor base + spread factor full cams_s0 + spread factor margin + spread factor full_no_cams ERA5-trained, stage 0 onto ERA5, spread factor (drops the CAMS-trained pair of training and stage 0 target) n/a full_no_s0 cams + spread factor n/a

Dropping the spread factor from the full stack gives cams_s0 (solar) and margin (wind). Dropping the base margin from the wind stack gives base_spread.

docs.title: Planned contrasts
docs.text:
The experiment plans 12 contrasts. Each is the arm named first minus the arm named second, scored per technology.

Id Solar Id Wind S1 full - base (headline) W1 full - base (headline) S2 cams - base W2 margin - base S3 cams_s0 - cams W3 base_spread - base S4 base_spread - base W4 base_spread - full (drop the margin) S5 full_no_cams - full (drop CAMS) W5 margin - full (drop the spread factor) S6 full_no_s0 - full (drop stage 0) S7 cams_s0 - full (drop the spread factor)
